A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CircuitSense benchmark and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A.1–A.9. Content can be reliably matched across the title change and layout shifts.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of six MLLMs on perception, analysis, and design tasks, plus derivation-error and block-diagram representation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical evaluations and adds results for GPT-4o-mini and Gemma-3-27B, including the appendix representation comparison.

M1.justification: Section 2.2 retains the schematic and block-diagram generators, electrical-validity constraints, and symbolic ground-truth procedures. The added appendix prompt documents an existing task rather than establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same reported 8,006-problem collection, curated and synthetic sources, six hierarchy levels, and Perception/Analysis/Design tasks. The exact versus high-level block-diagram scenarios also remain unchanged.

E2.justification: GPT-4o-mini and Gemma-3-27B are added to the comparisons in Tables 2–6 and Appendix Table 8. All six original models remain, making this a limited extension of the existing comparison suite.

E3.justification: The evaluation procedures, dataset counts, symbolic-equivalence checks, simulation setup, and inference settings remain unchanged. Appendix A.5 retains temperature 0.1, maximum tokens 4096, and top-p 0.95. Newly documenting the block-diagram prompt does not establish a protocol revision.

E4.justification: Appendix A.1 extends the existing comparison of abstract block labels versus explicit transfer functions to the two added models, providing more evidence about topology versus algebraic difficulty. The 100-attempt failure analysis in Table 7 and the appendix case examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional model results retain the same point-accuracy reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 2–6 and 8 add results for two models; their synthetic overall accuracies are 3.76% for GPT-4o-mini and 3.84% for Gemma-3-27B. Table 2 revises GPT-4o connection-identification accuracy from 94% to 70% without reporting a setting change. Other retained table scores, including Gemini-2.5-Pro's 19.06% synthetic overall accuracy, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Mason's gain formula in Section 2.2 and the op-amp and PLL derivations in Appendix A.3 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, definitions, proofs, or theoretical results are added or revised.

C1.justification: The central claims about hierarchical benchmarking, the perception-to-symbolic-reasoning gap, and the relationship between symbolic reasoning and design capability are retained. Updating six evaluated models to eight describes expanded supporting evidence rather than a new core contribution.

C2.justification: Sections 4 and 7 and Appendix A.1 retain the interpretations concerning pattern matching, algebraic bottlenecks, and design capability, along with the synthetic-task and 12–15-component limitations. No substantive qualification is added to address the revised perception results.

D1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds identifiers for the two new models, and A.8 adds the block-diagram prompt. New Section 8 states that the dataset accompanies supplementary materials and generator code is available on GitHub; actual availability is not established by the PDFs. Its statement that A.8 provides the judge prompt is not supported by that appendix.

R1.justification: The introduction and Section 5 add EEE-Bench and MMCircuitEval, while the MMMU discussion and reference are removed. A Gemma 3 technical-report citation is added. The positioning around hierarchical symbolic derivation remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: The title changes from a circuit-system benchmark to an MLLM benchmark, publication headers and affiliation/contact details are edited, and the circuit-related-work paragraph is revised. Reproducibility and acknowledgments sections are added, while most prose and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 adds model traces and updates its legend, and the comparison tables gain rows. Appendix Table 8 and Figure 4 move from text-wrapped placements to separate centered displays, Table 9 is resized, and A.8 gains a prompt box. These are localized presentation changes.

improvement.justification: The additional model comparisons and disclosed block-diagram prompt make v2 more informative and better documented. However, Section 3.2 still claims 94–100% perception performance for GPT-4o despite Table 2 changing its connection score to 70%; GPT-4o-mini's 24% connection score also challenges the retained broad claims about closed-source perception. Section 8 additionally promises a judge prompt absent from A.8. Useful evidence and documentation coexist with worsened internal consistency, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
